name: Antinori Tignanello 2013
text:
## Antinori Tignanello 2013

**The story.** [Antinori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antinori) is one of the oldest family businesses in the world. Rinuccio di Antinoro was recorded making wine near [Calenzano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calenzano) in 1180, and in 1385 Giovanni di Piero Antinori joined Florence's Guild of Winemakers, the date usually taken as the start of the wine business. By 1506 the family could pay 4,000 florins for the [Palazzo Antinori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palazzo_Antinori) in Florence, and it later gained the title of marquis ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antinori)).

**The wine: Tignanello.** Tignanello is named after the Tenuta di Tignanello estate at [San Casciano in Val di Pesa](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Tenuta+Tignanello,+San+Casciano+in+Val+di+Pesa,+Italy&t=k) in Chianti Classico. Piero Antinori first made it in the early 1970s, and it broke the rules: it blended [Cabernet Sauvignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabernet_Sauvignon) and [Cabernet Franc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabernet_Franc) with the traditional [Sangiovese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangiovese), was aged in small French [barriques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_%28wine%29), and after 1975 dropped the white grapes then required by [Chianti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti) law. It therefore lost its DOC status and was sold as humble table wine until 1994. Wikipedia calls it an innovative pioneer of the "[Super Tuscans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscan_wine)" that "decisively shaped Italian viticulture" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tignanello)). The usual blend has been 80% Sangiovese, 15% Cabernet Sauvignon and 5% Cabernet Franc since 1995.

For 2013, the Wine Advocate reports that blend again, but with a key difference: the Tignanello vineyard, replanted around 15 years earlier, had reached "its production prime". Winemaker Renzo Cotarella told Monica Larner: "stylistically-speaking, this is what we wanted to achieve" ([JJ Buckley, critics' notes](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2013-antinori-tignanello-igt/2013-89-750)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Tuscany vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/tuscany) calls 2013 "a 'classic vintage'", harvested at the start of October as used to be normal. A cool, wet spring delayed budbreak by two weeks and a very wet May forced constant spraying, but "a picture-perfect July, August and September saved the year", giving "elegant, fresh wines, albeit with a certain austerity". Renzo Cotarella told Decanter it was one of the most vibrant Tignanellos Antinori has ever made.

**What the critics say for 2013.** As listed by [JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2013-antinori-tignanello-igt/2013-89-750):
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 97** (July 2016). Blackberry, black truffle, dried cherry and tobacco: "So complex on the nose. Almost no need to taste it." Full-bodied with soft, velvety tannins; "The mouthfeel is magic."
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 96** (Monica Larner, December 2016). "The beginning of a new chapter for Italy's ultimate game-changer wine": harmonious and beautifully integrated, with black fruit and baking spice.
- **[Decanter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decanter_%28magazine%29): 95**. Recalls 2010 in a slightly less powerful package; blackberry-bush Cabernet, dark earth, red cherry and minerality; long, refined tannins. "Currently austere rather than generous", it needed time.
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 95** (January 2020, from a vertical). Licorice and blackcurrant, "intense and harmonious", with excellent length and a mineral element. Best 2023 to 2043.
- **[Wine Enthusiast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Enthusiast): 94** (March 2017). Red woodland berry, new leather, Asian spice and menthol; firm acidity and polished, tightly wound tannins. "It will age majestically." Drink 2020 to 2033.
- **Wine & Spirits: 92** (April 2017). Blackcurrant and tobacco, vanilla and coconut from oak, and a long, smoky finish.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.8** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is thirteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2022 to 2035, and Wine Spectator's runs from 2023 to 2043. The austerity Decanter noted should have relaxed, so this is a fine time to open it: blackcurrant, cherry, licorice, tobacco and earth, with years to go. Decant an hour or two ahead and serve at about 17°C.

**Food.** Tuscan classics: [bistecca alla fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistecca_alla_fiorentina), roast lamb with rosemary, [pappardelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pappardelle) with wild boar ragù, or [Pecorino Toscano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecorino_toscano).

**Value and where to buy.** Tignanello is everywhere here. BC Liquor has the 2020 ($119.99 and $459.99 in different listings) and the 2022 ($189.99); BSW Liquor has the 2023 at $210; ZYN has the 2012 at $296, 2019 at $270, 2020 at $268, 2022 at $218 and 2023 at $208, plus its sister Solaia. For the 2013's own critical record, the current vintages are fairly priced by comparison.

**From the history books**
- **A murder in the family.** In 1576 Bernardino Antinori's affair with Dianora di Toledo, wife of Pietro de' Medici, ended in tragedy: Pietro strangled his wife, and Bernardino was arrested and killed in prison ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antinori)).
- **Etruscan roots.** Tuscan winemaking goes back to the [Etruscans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etruscan_civilization) in the 8th century BC; amphorae show Tuscan wine was exported to southern Italy and Gaul by the 7th century BC ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscan_wine)).
- **The Super Tuscans.** In the 1970s a new class of wines made outside the DOC rules, the "Super Tuscans", emerged; many became cult wines, and later reforms created the IGT category for them ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuscan_wine)).

**Curious details**
- **Table wine at luxury prices.** For over two decades Tignanello could only be labelled as table wine, until it gained IGT status in 1994 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tignanello)).
- **Primum Familiae Vini.** Antinori is a member of this club of the world's great family wine houses ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antinori)).
